def: public key that represents a trust authority, produced either from a single signing key or composed from multiple keys under a threshold scheme

multi-dimensional authorization boundary that defines the extent of a trust authority's signing power, carried as a signed field in every certificate and cryptographically enforced at every delegation link
executable predicate included in an authorization scope, evaluated at verification time against the content and context of a trusted artifact
one axis of an authorization scope, along which the scope is constrained independently of other dimensions

act of constraining one or more authorization scope dimension when delegating from a parent trust authority to a child, such that the child's authorization scope is a subset of the parent's scope on every dimension
deterministic byte-string representation of the artifact data that all co-signature attest
protocol by which a quorum of key holders cooperates to produce a threshold signing signature, including the procedural, logistical, and cryptographic steps

scheme-defined label assigned to a trusted artifact by applying the classification policy to the coverage report, reflecting the artifact's dimensional coverage, authorization scope validity, transparency inclusion, and revocation status
signature on the same canonical payload of a trusted artifact, produced by a signer from an independent trust dimension or an independent trust chain
single signature produced by the AND-composition of two or more signature algorithms over the same canonical payload

trust authority that has received signing authority through delegation from a parent trust authority and whose authorization scope is a subset of the parent's scope on every authorization scope dimension
co-signature tagged with a trust dimension type, attesting the canonical payload from the perspective of that dimension
property of a trusted artifact on which multiple trust dimension have attested, each independently verifiable
set of verified trust dimension attested on a trusted artifact, recorded in the coverage report as input to the classification policy
credential that authorizes a specific signing key to produce trusted artifact and that carries the narrowest scope in its trust chain
delegated trust authority whose members are independent organizations that cooperate under a threshold scheme to produce a single aggregate key
protocol by which independent mirror and verifiers cross-check their views of a transparency log by comparing fingerprints of log state
cryptographic proof (typically a Merkle audit path) that a trusted artifact or its end certificate is included in a transparency log
independent operator that replicates a transparency log and serves inclusion proofs and log entries to verifiers
property of a delegation chain whereby the child authorization scope is a subset of (or equal to) the parent scope on every authorization scope dimension at every delegation link
attestation model in which a trusted artifact or end certificate is included in at least M of K independent transparency log, where M and K are specified by the issuing authority's policy
machine-readable public projection of an end certificate or trusted artifact, optimized for compact storage and rapid presentation (for example, via a two-dimensional barcode)
pair of parameters (T, N) specifying that at least T of N members shall cooperate to produce a valid threshold signing signature
trust authority that serves as the root of a delegation hierarchy and defines the initial authorization scope under which all subordinate authorities operate

cryptographic protocol in which at least T of N designated key holders cooperate to produce a single aggregate signature under the group's aggregate key, without any individual holder possessing the full signing capability
signing key representing a time authority, used to produce a dimension attestation of type time
append-only, cryptographically verifiable log (typically a Merkle tree) that records all issued end certificate and trusted artifact for public audit
public key of a root trust authority that a verifier accepts as the starting point for verification paths in the trust graph
self-contained set of trust anchor (root aggregate key or their fingerprints) sufficient for offline verification of any trusted artifact within the bundle's recognized scope
entity that holds signing authority within a trust graph under an authorization scope, and is represented by an aggregate key
ordered sequence of delegations from a root trust authority through one or more delegated trust authority to an end certificate
independently verifiable aspect of reality attested by a co-signature on a trusted artifact
directed acyclic graph of all trust authority and their delegation relationships, generalizing the linear trust chain to admit multiple paths, cross-hierarchy edges, and federated trust authority
formal revocation of previously-granted trust, executed by authorized parties through threshold-gated revocation mechanisms, in response to key compromise, scope violation, or fraud
signed data object produced under the authorization of an end certificate, carrying one or more co-signature from one or more trust dimension

ordered sequence of checks applied to a trusted artifact, including signature validation, trust chain or trust graph path-finding, authorization scope enforcement, transparency log inclusion proof, revocation status, coverage report production, and classification policy application
